abstract: For five rational Diophantine entries, the classical factor-analysis pentad applied to their signed pair roots minus a common shift is quadratic in the shift. We prove a universal descent of its discriminant squareclass, retaining all ten original root relations and allowing all five entries to vary independently. Changing root signs on any four-cycle preserves the nonzero squareclass. More explicitly, the six one-factorizations of $K_6$ index six polynomials $\Delta_{\mathcal T}$ with only 26 reduced radical characters each, compared with 416 for the original discriminant $D$. We give a compact matching formula and exact certificates $V_{\mathcal T}^2=D\Delta_{\mathcal T}$ whose sum is $D$. Thus whenever $D\ne0$, at least one descended representative is nonzero, and every nonzero representative has the same rational square status as $D$. The sign action gives 32 classes among 512 normalized root signings; the supplied classifier needs at most 32 square tests at every rational specialization, including vanishing discriminants and degenerate shifted polynomials. The identities are verified by independent characteristic-zero polynomial implementations, with a small standalone supplement. Local-series sign recovery and Kronecker substitution provide a practical discovery method, but are not assumptions of the proof. These results simplify a necessary low-rank representation condition; they do not construct a rational septuple or replace its individual pairwise square conditions.
